completed.notes: BOTH faces, against baseline's headless-only. Windowed proven in the GPU-less form the engine documents; a real window is impossible on this box (no display server). The build was clean FIRST TRY — the patch-table instructions were correct and sufficient — and it needed no `bevy` dependency, confirming slice B's claim.

run.first_engine_file_reason: To find where `RoomSpec` and `RoomMetadata` live. `ModuleDraft::playable` takes `Vec<RoomSpec>` and `ModuleDraft::room` takes `RoomMetadata`; neither was reachable from `ambition::app::prelude`, rustdoc with --no-deps rendered both as unlinked text, and rustc offered NO import suggestion for `RoomSpec`. CLOSED the same day: the prelude now re-exports both, guarded by `the_app_prelude_carries_the_room_types_its_signatures_require`.

where RoomSpec/RoomMetadata live (did not answer it)
why its host hung, and the character-roster RON schema

compared_to_baseline.first_file_opened: fixtures/external_consumer/Cargo.lock (a BUILDABILITY question) -> crates/ambition_world/src/lib.rs (an API question)
compared_to_baseline.reading: The first-file field moved from 'I cannot compile this' to 'I cannot find one type', which is the campaign working: the blocker got smaller and more specific. §4.2 still fails — the gate is ZERO engine files.

findings.severity: highest — cost the run real time
findings.summary: docs/sdk/ was last touched at c01d771bd while slices B and C landed no_characters/no_audio/playable/host_status/EMPTY_CHARACTER_ROSTER_RON/world::prelude/minimal_game. Its 'Known gaps' actively claimed a minimal module CANNOT reach a windowed host and that there is NO way to ask whether the game started. Both were false at HEAD.
findings.agents_words: a doc advertising gaps that no longer exist does the same thing
findings.why_it_matters: The README's own thesis is that hiding gaps sends readers into crates/. Advertising phantom gaps is the same defect wearing the opposite sign, and it was introduced by the campaign that wrote the thesis.

findings.summary: A `starting_character` no roster contained was accepted by try_build; 120 ticks ran, the process exited 0, the host never started. The agent flagged it as a FALSE POSITIVE against itself and only caught it by adding host_status.
findings.agents_words: the exact silent-failure shape slice A closed for routes, left open for characters
findings.fix: Validated at build; refusal names the character and lists the ones that exist. Test: a_starting_character_no_roster_contains_is_refused_at_build.

findings.summary: 'not registered by any mounted capability' sent the agent looking for how to write a capability plugin; the actual fix is `playable()`. The message also carried ~30 spaces of source indentation into its output.
findings.fix: Indentation fixed. Naming `playable` as the likely fix is still open.

findings.summary: no_characters() exists but playable() requires a starting character, and without playable() no gameplay route is registered. A menu-only app cannot compose. Now stated in the SDK's Known gaps and asserted by declaring_no_cast_and_a_starting_character_is_refused.

`ambition::bevy` is re-exported without Bevy's `debug` feature, so World::inspect_entity reports '<Enable the debug feature to see the name>' for everything — removing the one generic tool a consumer has for 'what did the engine spawn?'.
EMPTY_CHARACTER_ROSTER_RON covers the empty case; a game with ONE character is the actual minimal case and every required field is undocumented. The agent copied a fixture verbatim.

what_worked: The patch-table paragraph: 'accurate, prominent, and load-bearing — my build resolved and compiled first try because of it.' That was blind run 1's top finding, closed, and confirmed closed by run 2.
try_build's composition errors: 'genuinely good (three problems named at once, each with its consequence)'.
A minimal game needs exactly one dependency. The claim held under an independent build.
run.verdict: Both faces reached, engine surfaces read halved, and the blocker moved from 'cannot compile' to 'cannot locate one type'. §4.2 still fails: the gate is ZERO engine files and this run opened one.

criteria.evidence: Untouched, and NOT slice A's to touch. The barrier is process-global: Mary-O, Sanic, the versus fighters and the robot lineage all still stage through it, so an Outlander-only slice cannot make it deletable. This is the criterion whose misplacement forced the campaign's A-D split.

⚠ RECLASSIFIED 2026-07-30. Previously marked composition/deletable on the strength of the green hand-ordering contract. That contract is about HOST composition order; this criterion is about CONTENT completeness, which is still decided by `Plugin::build` running `install_outlander_content` and by the finish/PreStartup apparatus slice A never went near. `define` accumulating into a draft is the shape that will close it, but the draft holds routes and a room in slice A, not content.
content-model criterion; the idempotence flag is untouched (slice B+)

⚠ MOVED AWAY from deletable, and this is the sharpest thing slice A measured. `PlatformerApp` gained `with_game_assets`, OFF by default on headless and always on for windowed — so the two faces now consume different prepared art unless the consumer says otherwise. That was a deliberate correction (the first draft installed assets on both faces citing THIS criterion, and the fixture's rollback parity test caught it: under GGRS the extra asset frames are frames the sim does not advance, and the two hosts landed twelve `update()` calls apart). Preparing art is also not free — boot decode was measured at 627MP/2.5GB. So the knob is right and the criterion is further away, which is a real finding rather than a regression: the criterion wants ONE FINGERPRINT, and slice A has no content fingerprint to share. Slice B owns closing it, and must close it without collapsing the policy back into the face.
content-model criterion; no module-qualified namespaces exist yet (slice B)
content-model criterion; the fallback catalog is untouched (slice B)

capability_footprint.note: The consumer declares two dependencies (`ambition`, `bevy`) and links the whole engine closure. A module allowlist cannot see this: slice A's ratchet went from 18 to 14 while this number did not move at all, which is precisely the blind spot §2e exists to record.

minimal_game.verdict: The consumer-matrix question — does a small game link menus, persistence, audio, bosses? — is answered YES. A movement-only game with one room, one walker and no combat links 41 Ambition crates, 19 of which it never asked for: menus, persistence, cutscenes, encounters, inventory UI, portals, projectiles, LDtk, settings menus and touch input among them.
minimal_game.authorises_a_carve: NOT YET. §4 authorises an internal carve when a sentinel consumer's footprint cannot be reduced WITHOUT moving code between crates. This measurement shows the footprint is large; it does not show it is irreducible, because feature-gating has not been attempted. Trying that is the cheap experiment that either closes this or converts it into the carve argument — and §4 warns explicitly not to let a single leak authorise a full decomposition.
